name: Forty Floors of Bad Decisions
creator: Twin Palms Media Collective (Rashida Okonkwo-Brandt and Vikram Czekalski)
description: A weekly comedy podcast hosted by longtime friends Rashida Okonkwo-Brandt (Tier 3 accountant with illegal cosmetic geneware) and Vikram Czekalski (Tier 2 transit worker with a secondhand BCI two generations out of date), who discuss the absurdities of daily life in GLMZ with affectionate brutality. The show's format alternates between structured comedy bits, extended improvised arguments about minor civic failures, and occasional segments where listeners submit their worst recent interactions with corponation customer service. Their chemistry is widely cited as the reason the show works.
medium: neural feed audio / standard audio stream
cultural_impact: The show normalized cross-tier comedy perspectives for a broad working and middle-class audience, and its recurring segment 'Chrome on a Budget' — reviewing affordable augmentations with cheerful pessimism — became one of the most forwarded audio segments on neutral feed networks.
controversy: A 2213 episode joking about the Shelf's water filtration failures drew criticism from Tier 1 advocates who felt the humor minimized a genuine crisis; Okonkwo-Brandt and Czekalski addressed it directly in the next episode and donated the episode's listener revenue to a Shelf infrastructure mutual aid fund.
story_hooks: The show accidentally goes viral in Tier 4 circles after a bit about corponation customer service is interpreted as sophisticated satire; suddenly Rashida and Vikram are being courted by corporate media and neither of them wants it.

A listener submission for the customer service segment contains what sounds like a veiled description of an actual crime — and the hosts have to decide whether to report it or protect listener anonymity.
Vikram's outdated BCI begins causing minor audio artifacts in recordings that listeners start treating as intentional comedy bits; the hardware is slowly failing and he can't afford the upgrade.
